7.  Cabrillo Mole Rehabilitation Phase II Pre-Construction Stage 0 - Temporary Facility Site
  Preparation and Utility Installation Construction Change Order #1
  In July, Southern California Edison provided their energy requirements to serve the new
  Cabrillo Mole facility . After review of the plan , Jordahl Construction , Inc. submitted a
  request for a construction change order for $102 ,835. Staff evaluated the proposal and
  concluded that the price is reasonable . Furthermore, it was concluded that a competitive
  bid process would not only delay completion of the work, it would result in potential high
  costs due to the addition of mobilization costs.
  Recommended Action
  1. Make the affirmative finding, pursuant to Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4 .111(c) ,
  that a competitive market does not exist and the city will not gain a competitive advantage
  by competitively bidding this work. 2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the first
  amendment to the construction contract between Jordahl Construction , Inc. for the
  Cabrillo Mole Rehabilitation Phase II Pre-Construction Stage 0 - Temporary Facility Site
  Preparation and Utility Installation Project for a not-to-exceed sum of $110 ,000 fo r a total
  contract price of $1 ,360 ,000 .

8.  Slater Waterproofing , Inc. WWTP Grit Chamber Contract Construction Change Order

  repa irs at the City's waste water treatment plant, they've noticed the need fo r repairs to
  the digester deck walkway. The work to be performed includes repairs to spalled concrete
  along the digester deck.
  Recommended Action
  1. Make the affirmative finding , pursuant to Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.111 (c) ,
  that a competitive market does not exist and the city will not gain a competitive advantage
  by competitively bidding this work. 2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the first
  amendment to the short-form construction contract with Slater Waterproofing , Inc.
  increasing the contract sum by $89 ,000 for a not-to-exceed total sum of $214,000 .

SUBJECT:  Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Fourth Quarter Treasurer's Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION($): Adopt the resolution accepting the FY25-26 Fourth Quarter
Treasurer's Report.

REPORT SUMMARY: State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within
30 days following each fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City's cash and investment
balances. Attached is the Fourth Quarter Treasurer's Report for FY25-26 . The report was
shared with the City Treasurer prior to presentation to City Council.

The purpose of the report is to inform , on a quarterly basis, the City's cash and investment
balances, the investment types, yields , and market values , and to ensure that the City's
investments are in compliance with the City's adopted investment policy. In general , operating
cash is held in US Bank checking accounts and any excess cash is invested in California 's
Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) and various certificates of deposit (CDs) .

In accordance with Government Code sections 16429.1 and 53601 et seq., the City cannot
invest more than 30% of its portfolio in CDs. CDs accounted for 21 .9% of the unrestricted cash
and investments for the quarter ended June 30 , 2026. The City had three CDs and a United
States Treasury Bill mature during the quarter. The City takes a ladder approach with
staggered maturities for its CD investments to balance its goals of high rates in the short-term
with stability to withstand market fluctuations in the longer-term . Similarly , the City reinvested
$5 million of the United State Treasury Bill , which matured during the quarter, into another the
United State Treasury Bill with a maturity date of November 30, 2026. The City reinvested
these funds in a shorter term investment to ensure adequate liquidity during construction of the
Cabrillo Mole Ferry Terminal. While the project remains primarily grant-funded , the City will
need to initially finance portions of the construction with grant funds to be received on a
reimbursement basis. The City will continue to assess for opportunities to increase its
investment returns while maintaining necessary liquidity and compliance with its investment
policy.

During the fourth quarter 2026, two certificates of deposit using different brokers but from the
same financial institution, in violation of the City's Investment Policy. Upon identifying the error,
one CD was sold and reinvested with a different institution to restore compliance. While the
Finance Director is currently authorized under the policy to reinvest maturing CDs on behalf of
 the City, City Staff has modified its internal procedures to require written approval from the City
Treasurer prior to any future reinvestment of funds .

The unrestricted cash balance for the fourth quarter of 2025-2026 totaled $24 .81 million , a
decrease of $866 thousand from the fourth quarter of 2024-2025 . The decrease in unrestricted
cash balance is largely attributable to increased capital outlays during the current fiscal year,
with significant grant reimbursements outstanding at the end of the quarter. The City
experienced stronger visitor-driven tax revenues than expected during the quarter which
partially offset the decrease in cash from outstanding grant reimbursements . The unrestricted
cash balance also includes cash from enterprise funds (e.g . Harbor, Sewer, Saltwater, and
Solid Waste) not available for general government functions . While the majority of grant
funding is performed on a cash reimbursement basis , the unrestricted cash and investments
balance also includes approximately $1 million in grant pre-funding received for the Cabrillo
Mole Ferry Terminal Rehabilitation , with $X spent on mole substructure improvements and
temporary facilities as of June 30, 2026 (referred to as Project Stage 0 in prior staff reports) .
The City expects significant capital outlays on several major capital projects , including the
second phase of the Cabrillo Mole Ferry Terminal rehabilitation , the South Beach Seawall
Restoration , and the Green Pleasure Pier Decking Improvements, which will reduce the
unrestricted cash balances over the next several quarters.

disembarkment/embarkment, and serves as the primary entry point to the City of Avalon . In

and structures to improve passenger queuing and adjacent transportation circulation.

In order to accommodate sustained , mostly uninterrupted operations of the Cabrillo Mole ,
construction of the new facility has been broken into construction stages for bidder consid eration .
The Pre-Construction Stage - Stage O - includes four steps :

1. Purchase of long-lead equipment associated with the upgraded utility system .
2. Purchase temporary facilities .
3. Installation of grates at the old steamer ramp.
4. Installation of utility systems and other temporary infrastructure to support the future Cab rillo
  Mole facility as well as temporary facilities .
 The scope of work for installation of upgraded utility systems to support the new facility as well
as utilities to support temporary facilities that will be used during the construction project was
awarded to Jordahl Construction , Inc. on February 16, 2026 for a not to exceed sum of
